title: systemTest (Schemathesis): verify-by-hash must not resolve to an arbitrary registration — anchored-ancestor + cross-tenant field disclosure (KS-584 class)
description:
## Status: parked — not actionable yet

**Blocked on** [KS-584](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-584/verify-by-hash-selects-the-wrong-registration-certified-documents) (Kamil, Urgent). That ticket has to decide *what correct resolution means* before a regression can assert it — Stuart offered three candidate shapes (prefer a row carrying chain data · return the anchored ancestor · report ambiguity) and they produce three different assertions. Writing tests now would pin a behaviour nobody has chosen.

Filed so the systemTest leg is visible from [KS-492](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-492/review-g-systemtest-security-regression-coverage) rather than forgotten when [KS-584](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-584/verify-by-hash-selects-the-wrong-registration-certified-documents) lands. **No work until the platform decision is made.**

## Why it belongs in Review G

[KS-584](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-584/verify-by-hash-selects-the-wrong-registration-certified-documents) has two consequences from one root cause, and G already owns regression coverage for both classes:

**1. Anchored-ancestor selection.** `POST /api/verification/verify` resolves a content hash with `ORDER BY d.certified_at DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1` and no preference for a row carrying chain data (`services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts`). The normal certify flow creates a *second* row with the same `content_hash` (the certification's `signed_document`), which wins the ordering and carries no `certification_metadata.blockchain`. So a document with three confirmed on-chain anchors verifies with `isAnchored: false`, `blockHeight: null` — reproduced live on UAT (`1.15412159T20251122.pdf`, `f4fd83a9…`, anchors at preview blocks 4547897 / 4547901 / 4547907).

This is the **anchor-honesty class** — the same shape as [KS-589](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-589/systemtest-anchor-honesty-consistency-a-mock-tx-tx-sim-hash-must-never) and the [KS-492](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-492/review-g-systemtest-security-regression-coverage) D rows. A document's on-chain proof exists and the platform reports it doesn't.

**2. Cross-tenant field disclosure.** `buildResponse` returns the selected row's `title`, `issuer` / `organization_name`, `documentId`, `status`, `certifiedAt` and the lineage chain. The fallback `crossTenantLookup` is also unscoped, also `LIMIT 1`. Verifying a document you legitimately hold can return **another tenant's filename and organisation name** — and the anonymous verify path has no caller identity, so it cannot scope.

This is the **A / BUG-ISOLATION-001 class** that [KS-513](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-513/systemtest-cross-tenant-cross-owner-document-isolation-regressions) covered for documents and api-keys. [KS-513](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-513/systemtest-cross-tenant-cross-owner-document-isolation-regressions) is Done, so there is no open ticket carrying it, and the verify family went public under [KS-442](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-442/make-the-verify-family-public-5-ops-gateway-relax-spec-security-ks-424) — the sweep reaches these operations today.

Note `platform_document_registry` is already `UNIQUE (content_hash, tenant_id)`. K models tenancy correctly here; verify just doesn't use it.

## Sketch — to be finalised once [KS-584](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-584/verify-by-hash-selects-the-wrong-registration-certified-documents) decides

Placement: cross-tenant assertions with the `@pytest.mark.isolation` siblings; anchor-resolution assertions in the anchoring-integrity Integration mode.

| # | Property | Assertion | Depends on |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | Certify does not un-anchor | Upload → anchor → certify → verify. `isAnchored` must stay true and the txHash must still resolve. Assert **after** certification propagates, not before — the UAT reproduction only appears once the second row exists | [KS-584](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-584/verify-by-hash-selects-the-wrong-registration-certified-documents) decision |
| 2 | Multiple registrations resolve deterministically | Two rows sharing a `content_hash` → verify must not return an arbitrary one. Exact assertion depends on which of the three shapes is chosen | [KS-584](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-584/verify-by-hash-selects-the-wrong-registration-certified-documents) decision |
| 3 | Ambiguity is not hidden | If the chosen shape is "report ambiguity", assert the match count / flag is present and a relying party can see it | Only if that shape wins |
| 4 | Anonymous verify discloses no tenant-owned fields | Register a document under tenant A; verify the same bytes anonymously → response carries no `title`, `organization_name`, `issuer` or lineage belonging to A | **Independent of the** [KS-584](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-584/verify-by-hash-selects-the-wrong-registration-certified-documents) **decision** — this one could be written now if the disclosure half is ruled on separately |
| 5 | Cross-tenant fallback is scoped | A caller with a tenant does not silently receive another tenant's registration via `crossTenantLookup` | [KS-584](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-584/verify-by-hash-selects-the-wrong-registration-certified-documents) decision |

Test 4 is the only row that does not wait on the resolution semantics — the disclosure question ("should an anonymous verify name an organisation at all?") is separable, and Stuart's framing is that it can honestly answer *registered / integrity intact / not revoked / anchored yes-no* without naming anyone.

## Out of scope

Everything platform-side — row selection, tenant scoping, and what an anonymous response may contain — is [KS-584](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-584/verify-by-hash-selects-the-wrong-registration-certified-documents)**, Kamil's**. This ticket only proves the outcome once chosen. Platform-S consumption ([PS-546](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-546/verify-shows-a-permanent-for-certification-and-never-reports-anchoring) / [PS-547](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-547/share-link-verify-re-derives-the-document-by-hash-so-a-duplicate)) is Stuart's and not tracked here.

## References

[KS-584](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-584/verify-by-hash-selects-the-wrong-registration-certified-documents) (platform defect, Kamil, Urgent — the blocker) · [KS-492](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-492/review-g-systemtest-security-regression-coverage) (Review G parent) · [KS-486](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-486/review-a-authn-authz-tenancy-and-idor) (Review A) · [KS-513](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-513/systemtest-cross-tenant-cross-owner-document-isolation-regressions) (the closed isolation ticket this class belonged to) · [KS-589](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-589/systemtest-anchor-honesty-consistency-a-mock-tx-tx-sim-hash-must-never) (anchor honesty — sibling class) · [KS-442](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-442/make-the-verify-family-public-5-ops-gateway-relax-spec-security-ks-424) (verify family made public) · [KS-478](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-478/ks-466-11-state-machineprecondition-400s-resolve-via-ks-188-stateful) (red→green rule) · [PS-546](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-546/verify-shows-a-permanent-for-certification-and-never-reports-anchoring) / [PS-547](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-547/share-link-verify-re-derives-the-document-by-hash-so-a-duplicate) (S-side consumers, merged).

Evidence is Stuart's UAT reproduction and Kamil's root-cause read on [KS-584](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-584/verify-by-hash-selects-the-wrong-registration-certified-documents). Not independently re-verified by me; nothing written.

nodes.title: Refs KS-590: a verify withholds another customer's details on all four paths

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** Built as ruled (card secuura-backlog-31-decisions-1109 = a, pack row 16, option 1, "withhold all four") in PR 2138, head fdf80425e9d5 after fix round 1, not merged. An anonymous verify, or one from another tenant, no longer reveals the title, the issuer, certifiedBy, the certifier's organisation id or the on-chain metadata. This holds on every answer that names a registration: v1 by hash, by document id and by file, both chain-first answers and their draft/revoked downgrade, and v2's chain-only match. The verdict, the checks, the anchor facts and the certification's id, type and time are unchanged.

- **All four gaps re-read at develop f98afb113c2d before the edit, and all four still held.**
  - Organisation id: the scrub never nulled it. It was nulled only on the KS 1986 foreign-original path.
  - Chain-first: both answers returned directly with issuer, org id and the whole onChainMetadata. The /verify downgrade did the same with a local title.
  - No tenancy info: such a row was never scrubbed.
  - By id: the two local by-id reads selected no tenant_id.
- **Behaviour change.**
  - A caller still sees its own tenant's rows named. In production an anonymous caller is the default tenant, so a single-tenant deployment (demo, local) reads its own rows as before.
  - The visible change: a hash known only to the chain still verifies, but no longer names its issuer. The anchored transaction's own metadata stays public on Cardano.
  - Rows with no tenant cannot exist on a database that ran migration 011, which made documents.tenant_id NOT NULL (the tier-1 gate measured it on PostgreSQL 15). That is the guarantee behind the no-tenant rule; I had credited migration 039's row-level security, which binds only some database roles.
- **Proof.**
  - 26 new cells (3 added in fix round 1): 19 red on develop exactly as predicted, 7 controls green, 26 green with the change.
  - 12 of 12 mutants killed, each reddening exactly its declared cells, including the two the tier-1 gate found surviving.
  - Three existing cells pinned the old disclosure and were updated, each named in the PR: the ks584 legacy-row cell, the ks563 certified cell and ks1939 C2.
  - originate suite 2,592 of 2,592 before, 2,618 of 2,618 after (Node v26.8.1, not an LTS line). The tier-1 gate also ran the KS 1114 T9 integration golden: 17 of 17 on PostgreSQL 15.
- **Also in the PR, granted by our coordinator:** v2's chain-only match (gap 2's v2 door) and the chain-answer example in docs/VERIFICATION.md.
- **Deploy:** per Kam's card secuura-ks590-verify-disclosure-four-questions-1102 = a, verifiers including Platform S stop seeing the org id, so a deploy needs Kam's word to Stuart first. The merge to develop does not.
- **Not run:** the four platform suites, two DB-gated integration suites, a live chain-first proof (it needs a real 64-hex tx in anchor_store), Node 24, demo.

It goes to a tier-1 gate next: https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/2138

_Edited 2026-11-09 for fix round 1 (tier-1 gate 292): the head, the migration-011 correction, the counts and the deploy line. The original text said migration 039._

**BLUF:** Kam ruled the 31-decision card `secuura-backlog-31-decisions-1109` on 2026-11-09 at 13:44:07 (live board), in these words: "Decision secuura-backlog-31-decisions-1109: a — All recommendations (A and B)". Option a reads: "Every row ruled as recommended; a board seat files and moves the tickets; the KS-607 demo rows still wait for a separate yes." This ticket is row A16 of the decision pack, ruled as recommended: option 1. Withhold all four disclosures from an anonymous verify: the organisation's id, the two chain-first answers that skip the scrub, old rows with no tenant, and lookups by document id. A build seat makes the code match, and a test then checks it.

The four gaps come from a code reading on 2026-08-11 and were still open on 2026-10-06; they were not re-read at the current develop. A build seat does the work; nothing was changed in code by this comment.

Alongside this comment the ticket, which was unassigned, is assigned to the board account, and moves from Backlog to Todo.

## Status check 2026-10-06: not parked any more; four disclosure questions still need Kamil

**BLUF:** The "parked — not actionable yet" header is out of date. KS-584 is **Deployed to UAT**, and the `/api/v2/verification/verify` contract is in the published spec on `develop` (`docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`, the KS-1133 notes around `:6446` and `:6565`). Rows 1, 2 and 5 can be written against v1 now, and row 3 against v2. What's still missing is an answer to the four disclosure questions from the 08-11 comment. Kamil's 08-12 reply covered the v2 shape but not those four:

1. `certification.certifierOrganizationId` survives `scopeTenantFields`. Does an org UUID count as tenant-owned naming?
2. Both chain-first branches return directly and skip `scopeTenantFields`.
3. `isCrossTenantResponse` returns `false` for rows with no tenancy info, so legacy rows are never scrubbed.
4. The by-id path selects no `tenant_id`, so it is never scoped.

**@kamil.kreiser:** could you rule on those four? Each one changes what row 4 asserts, and they're platform decisions; a test shouldn't settle them on its own.

>>> Detail

* **Related.** KS-1119 (Backlog, Kamil): `crossTenantLookup`'s by-documentId fallback can answer `verified: true` for a wrong hash. That's the same code path as row 5. Row 5 should either include it as a case or explicitly leave it out.
* **The 08-11 note on mock stacks still applies.** The chain-first branch can't be reached without a real 64-hex tx in `anchor_store`. Measure that before choosing between a test and a report.
* No PR is open, and nothing has been written yet.

Checked against `origin/develop` `f556373b9`. Read-only.

>>>

Refs as KS-NNN text. Posted by agent on Peter's behalf.

## Unparking check 2026-08-12 (agent, grounded against develop `52368d8c3`)

**The blocker this ticket was parked behind has moved.** [KS-584](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-584) is now *In Review* with two merges on develop:

- **[#662](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/662) (interim, `2026-08-11`)** — "verify-by-hash answers from the row that evidences its claims; tenant fields scoped".
- **[#666](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/666) (P3, `89ed853a7`, `2026-08-12`)** — the **`/v2` verify-list contract**: multiplicity dissolves row selection, anchor truth caller-independent. v1 verify unchanged; deploy waits on Kintsugi.

So the ticket's premise — *"that ticket has to decide what correct resolution means before a regression can assert it"* — no longer holds. Of Stuart's three candidate shapes, the landed answer is closest to **"report ambiguity"**, taken further: `/v2` returns the list rather than picking, and the interim fix already makes v1 prefer the evidencing row and scope tenant fields.

**Consequences for the sketch table:**

| # | Property | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Certify does not un-anchor | waiting on decision | **assertable** — interim [#662](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/662) fixes v1 row choice; assert on v1 after certification propagates |
| 2 | Multiple registrations resolve deterministically | waiting on decision | **shape changed** — on `/v2` this is no longer "which row wins" but "the list is complete and caller-independent" |
| 3 | Ambiguity is not hidden | conditional | **applies** — that is effectively what `/v2` does; assert the list surfaces every match |
| 4 | Anonymous verify discloses no tenant-owned fields | already independent | unchanged — still the row that could always have been written |
| 5 | Cross-tenant fallback is scoped | waiting on decision | **assertable** — [#662](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/662) claims tenant fields are now scoped; this is the regression that proves it |

**Two caveats before treating this as fully unblocked:**

1. KS-584 is *In Review*, **not Done** — the contract could still move. Rows 2/3 in particular pin `/v2` shape.
2. Coverage must be explicit about **which version it asserts against**. v1 and `/v2` now answer differently by design; a test that does not say which it means will look right and prove nothing. Note also the BACKLOG ruling item carried on [#666](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/666) — *verify-file 415-gated at the gateway (v1+v2)* — found during the P3 live proof.

Nothing written; this is a re-grounding of the park, not a start. Refs: [KS-584](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-584) · [KS-492](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-492) (Review G parent) · [KS-589](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-589) (sibling anchor-honesty class) · [KS-513](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-513) (closed isolation ticket this class belonged to).

## BLUF
**The P3 /v2 contract your tests can pin is now ready-to-land** (draft PR [#666](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/666), holding for Kam's cutover word) — this note is so your KS-590 regression work can target both shapes without re-deriving them.

## What v2 gives this ticket
- `POST /api/v2/verification/verify` → `{hash, count, matches[]}` — **no selection at all**: the arbitrary-registration class this ticket exists for cannot recur in v2, and the assertable invariant is structural: every same-hash registration appears; `matches[0].documentId` equals v1's answer for the same hash (deterministic order: certified by ms-precise certified_at DESC → real confirmed tx → in-flight → oldest created).
- **Cross-tenant field disclosure** (your title's second class): scoped matches null tenant-owned naming AND carry an explicit `fieldsWithheld: true` — so a regression can assert withholding directly instead of inferring it from nulls.
- **Anchor truth is caller-independent by construction**: the chain-fact read is pre-auth and v2 forwards no bearer. Assertable as: v2 response (modulo verifiedAt) identical with and without a valid bearer — `scripts/verify/ks584-p3-parity-sweep.mjs` already sweeps exactly this (60/60 local groups clean; read-only, works against any env).
- Auth posture for your harness: absent bearer → 200; present-but-invalid → **401** (this also fixed a pre-existing raw-500 on malformed bearers — the not_a_server_error class — details on KS-584).
- The spec op (`/api/v2/verification/verify`, security: [], inline example) is in `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` on the branch, so Schemathesis picks it up at cutover.

v1 stays untouched until cutover, so your v1 pins (per your 08-11 comment) carry no churn risk and stay valid afterwards too.

## BLUF — this ticket is no longer blocked; the decision it was parked on now exists in code and in Kamil's written ruling

This ticket says *"parked — not actionable yet … Writing tests now would pin a behaviour nobody has chosen."* That was correct when filed. It is no longer true, and I want the evidence recorded here so the next person doesn't re-derive it.

**Nothing written, nothing verified by me beyond reading the merged code and his design notes.**

## 1. The row-selection decision has been made and is merged

The KS-584 interim merged to `develop` (#662, `d0a704d57`) and is live. `selectVerifiableRow` (`services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts:190`) implements a **deterministic** precedence, replacing the `ORDER BY certified_at DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1` this ticket describes:

1. a `certified` row (most recent, since the SQL pre-sorts `certified_at DESC`);
2. else a row with a **real** 64-hex tx (`rowHasRealTx`, excluding `simulated: true`), confirmed-first then oldest `created_at`;
3. else the oldest row.

Rowset is `LIMIT VERIFY_ROWSET_LIMIT` (24, `:276`). Certification evidence is now read across the whole same-hash set via `siblingCertification` (`:206`), and `confirmStalePendingAnchor` (`:279`) heals a stale pending anchor at read time.

So sketch rows **1, 2 and 5** have a defined behaviour to assert. Row 3 ("report ambiguity") did **not** win — the chosen shape is deterministic selection, not surfaced multiplicity.

## 2. Kamil's P3 ruling means pinning v1 carries no churn risk

This was my main worry, and his own notes resolve it. From `Blockchain/Dev/docs/design/2026-08-11_p3-verify-list-design.md` on his parked branch `feature/ks-584-p3-versioned-verify-list-caller-independent-anchor-truth`:

> **"Versioned coordinated cutover. v1 single-doc verify shape UNTOUCHED until Stuart adopts."**
> **"v1 keeps the interim's selection logic (already deterministic + honest post-KS-584-interim)."**

P3 adds `POST /api/v2/verification/verify` returning `{ matches: [...], count, hash }` **alongside** v1 — *"No LIMIT-1 selection at all — the selection problem dissolves."* It is not a rewrite of v1. **Assertions against v1 are therefore safe to write now.**

Two further ruled constraints that shape the tests:

- **"Anonymous verify stays a supported public 200 path."** So row 4 must assert what an anonymous verify may *disclose* — never that it is refused.
- **"Anchor truth must be caller-independent."** This is a P3 *goal*, not current behaviour, and its delivery mechanism is an anchoring-side reconciler. An anon-vs-authed parity assertion written today would pin something the platform does not yet do — that one **should** still wait, or land as a strict Known Failure only if he wants it pinned.

His own validation plan is also a ready-made test shape: *"All duplicate-hash groups on demo (12+), not a sample: script the sweep (readonly) comparing v1 vs v2 answers per group + anchor-truth parity authenticated vs anonymous."*

## 3. Row 4 is narrower than this ticket assumes — and two disclosure gaps are NOT covered by the interim

The interim added `scopeTenantFields` (`:260-271`), but it nulls **only** `title`, `issuer`, and `certification.certifiedBy`. From a code read (not probed):

- **`certification.certifierOrganizationId` survives scoping** (`buildCertification`, `:141`) — a scoped verify still names the registering organisation by id. Whether an org UUID counts as tenant-owned naming is Kamil's call, not something a test should silently decide.
- **Both chain-first branches bypass `scopeTenantFields` entirely** (`:554-587` verify-file, `:982-1014` `/verify`): they `return res.json({...})` directly, emitting `onChainMetadata` wholesale plus `issuer` / `certifiedBy` / `certifierOrganizationId` from `chain.metadata`. Guarded by `rows.length === 0`, so reachable only for a hash on chain but absent from the local `documents` table.
- **`isCrossTenantResponse` returns `false` when the row has no tenancy info** (`:255`), so legacy rows are never scrubbed.
- **The by-id path rowset (`:1094-1099`) selects no `tenant_id`**, so that path is never scoped at all. Reachable on any stack — potentially the more serious of the four.

## 4. Practical note for whoever picks this up

On a **mock** stack the chain-first branch is unreachable: `anchor_store` holds no real 64-hex tx, so `GET /api/anchors/verify/{hash}` can never answer `verified: true`. A strict xfail on an unprovisionable vector would score absence as a result. Measure the real-tx count first and let it decide test-vs-report.

Also worth knowing: `GET /api/anchors/verify/{hash}` is **absent from the published OpenAPI spec**, so the sweep never touches it — the only existing coverage is one negative case (unknown hash → 404) in `test_anchor_verify_no_fabrication.py`.

## Recommendation

Un-park rows 1, 2 and 5 against v1 now. Hold the caller-independence assertion for P3. Put questions 3's four disclosure items to Kamil before encoding any of them — they are platform decisions wearing a test costume.

Sourced from the merged KS-584 interim and Kamil's parked P3 design notes, both read 2026-08-11. Not independently verified against a live stack; no code or tests written.
